answer: Copying the same citations across 263 aliases therefore forfeits the authoring cost 263 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the juniper index resolves every citation against the horizon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the velvet audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4974 identities would post 2695 proofs and burn roughly 46 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
